blocks.text: Joshua 14 contains 15 verses. It opens with: And these are the inheritances which the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers' `houses' of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed unto them, It concludes with: Now the name of Hebron beforetime was Kiriath-arba; `which Arba was' the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Joshua moves from succession and entry through campaigns to land allotment, tribal unity, farewell, and covenant renewal.
